dependencyGate.transitiveGate: T07 requires accepted T06; T15 requires accepted T06 and T14; T16 requires accepted T14/T15 and T06 canonical DTO/migration foundations.
dependencyGate.beforeGate: Only synthetic fixture/interface planning is prepared. Do not implement Rust outbox/repository/sync behavior, connect a fake-success backend, run tests/builds, or claim SQLCipher, crypto, DTO, PostgreSQL, ACK, cursor, or snapshot acceptance before dependencies and required contracts are accepted.

harnessBoundary.syntheticInputs: Use only symbolic profiles A/B, workspaces WA/WB, devices D1/D2, entities E1/E2, opaque wire/body/blob canaries, synthetic revisions/sequences/epochs, and synthetic receipts. Canaries are storage bytes only, not valid AEAD, crypto vectors, user content, or server success evidence.
plannedHarnesses: After T07 acceptance, use disposable SQLCipher databases and the T07 local repository/object fixtures to inject transaction failures and inspect durable rows/refcounts without live profiles or plaintext reports.
After T06/T15/T16 acceptance, use frozen DTOs and the real T16 isolated sync integration harness; no success-shaped fake server may stand in for a receipt, push, pull, ACK, or lease result.

For snapshot recovery, use only a frozen snapshot-page/catchup contract and isolated disposable namespaces. T19/server snapshot integration is separately gated; this plan does not assume a snapshot endpoint or provider result exists.
forbidden: Live profiles, real accounts/workspaces/devices, production/shared services, user data, credentials, key material, valid crypto vectors, or clipboard/input interaction.
Running implementation, behavior tests, builds, migrations, database/services, or measurements before T07/T15/T16 acceptance.
Treating cancellation, a missing receipt, an HTTP response, a mock transport, or a static plan as proof that a cloud mutation did or did not commit.
Changing immutable wire bytes/opId/baseRevision/nonce after possible delivery; auto-rebasing a sent op; dropping drafts/outbox on conflict, epoch/lease failure, budget pressure, or account switch.
Inventing DTO encoding/hash, ACKED row lifetime, conflict/merge policy, local byte accounting, or retry timing where the specification leaves it open.

syntheticActors.note: Actors and bytes are symbolic test inputs only. No real identity, secret, valid encryption output, server receipt, or user content is embedded.

cases.setup: Use WA/D1 with a synthetic cloud-scope mutation, opaque prepared wire bytes, and an isolated local database. Exercise a failure before commit and a restart after commit.
cases.action: Inspect the materialized record/draft, outbox row, ownership counters, and emitted success signal on both sides of the commit boundary.
assert: Before commit, the mutation has no durable partial record/outbox/counter effect and no success signal.
After commit, the record/draft and outbox are all durable together; UI success is emitted only after commit.
This fixture checks database transaction all-or-none behavior only; it does not claim power-loss/fsync guarantees until T07 freezes the database durability profile.

cases.setup: Prepare a synthetic record with newly owned body/original/thumbnail BLOBs and object references; inject a database failure while writing references, record, and outbox.
cases.action: Restart and inspect object ownership, references, pending byte counters, record, and outbox.
assert: A committed record cannot lack its owned BLOB/reference or matching outbox mutation.
A rolled-back mutation cannot leave a durable success record or an unreferenced pending source BLOB that appears committed.
No plaintext staging file is introduced; cloud staging remains a rebuildable cache from committed local bytes.

cases.setup: Create synthetic anonymous, A/WA, A/other-workspace, and B/WB namespaces with distinct records, drafts, and outbox rows.
cases.action: Switch active profile/account and request pending mutations and local keys for each namespace.
assert: A namespace switch cannot read, send, adopt, or acknowledge another namespace's outbox or key.
Anonymous local-only data remains separate from cloud-scoped data; account B cannot inherit A's pending mutations.
No namespace is deleted or merged as a side effect of switching.

references: 03 §6 outbox minimum columns and dependency rule
cases.setup: Create a synthetic saved draft whose referenced attachment dependency is not uploaded/ready, then expose a committed-ready dependency in an isolated fixture.
cases.action: Inspect outbox state and eligible sync operations before and after the dependency becomes ready.
assert: The blocked mutation is WAIT_DEPENDENCY while its dependency is not ready and does not claim a ready attachment reference.
Resolving the dependency can make the mutation eligible for preparation using the confirmed base revision; this does not exercise T18 upload behavior.
A failed dependency leaves the source draft and pending bytes available for recovery.

references: 03 §6 one in-flight wire op and draft chain
cases.setup: Prepare two offline edits to E1 while its first wire op is eligible and then possibly delivered; keep a separate E2 mutation eligible.
cases.action: Ask the sync engine to prepare/schedule eligible operations before and after E1's first receipt is confirmed.
assert: At most one possibly delivered wire operation for E1 exists at a time; later edits remain a persisted draft chain.
E2 can progress independently; E1's later operation is formed only after the prior operation is confirmed and a real revision is available.
A sent E1 operation is never merged into a later draft or silently replaced.

cases.setup: Persist a READY operation, mark it SENDING, simulate process termination before a result is durably acknowledged, then reopen the same isolated database.
cases.action: Read the recovered operation and make one retry request using the frozen DTO when available.
assert: A recovered SENDING operation returns to READY after restart.
Its opId, wire_bytes, wire_sha256, wire_size, epoch, and base_revision remain unchanged.
This local recovery does not infer whether the prior network request committed.

cases.setup: Mark a synthetic E1 operation as possibly delivered and retain its original opaque bytes and digest.
cases.action: Change a local draft, cursor, base revision, or request metadata and attempt to reuse the sent operation identity.
assert: The original operation bytes and identity are not edited to reflect a newer draft or revision.
A new wire operation requires the prior result/revision and a new operation identity; merge of a possibly sent operation is rejected.
The plan does not assert a specific local error code for the attempted edit.

cases.setup: Use a frozen T06/T16 synthetic create operation and active synthetic D1 lease; let the isolated server commit, then drop its response before the client persists the receipt.
cases.action: Restart the client and retry the same operation using the original serialized bytes.
assert: The retry reuses the same opId and exact bytes; the server receipt resolves to the original result/seq without a second version.
The client keeps the outbox row and draft until it durably records the receipt and confirmed revision/seq.
No receipt lookup result or absence is treated as proof that an ambiguous prior request failed.

references: 03 §7.1 push operation granularity and response order
cases.setup: Prepare independent synthetic operations for E1 and E2 in one batch; make one commit and one terminal rejection in the isolated T16 service.
cases.action: Deliver the response, interrupt local application between per-operation outcomes, and restart.
assert: Each operation outcome is reconciled independently; the batch is not treated as all-or-nothing.
A committed operation is not regenerated or resent as a new operation when another item fails.
An unconfirmed operation remains in durable local state with its original bytes.

cases.setup: Use synthetic network/5xx/429/TIMEOUT responses and a frozen retry policy; set maximum retry delay from syncRetryMaxSeconds=300 seconds.
cases.action: Advance the synthetic clock across retry attempts, including a response carrying Retry-After.
assert: Transient errors preserve the operation and exact bytes; retries do not mint new operation identities.
Retry-After is a lower bound where present, and retry delay does not exceed the configured maximum.
No immediate unbounded retry loop occurs; exact jitter distribution/attempt schedule is not asserted until frozen.

cases.setup: Seed one synthetic READY operation and deliver AUTH_REQUIRED, DEVICE_REVOKED, KEY_LOCKED, and QUOTA_EXCEEDED outcomes in separate runs.
cases.action: Resume the client after each outcome and inspect the operation, draft, and next eligible action.
assert: AUTH_REQUIRED retains the outbox while session recovery is required; DEVICE_REVOKED stops cloud sends; KEY_LOCKED waits for unlock.
Quota failure preserves the operation and does not silently switch its scope or discard local material.
No fixture claims a UI copy or unspecified local error code beyond the frozen protocol mapping.

cases.setup: Start E1 at confirmed revision r. D1 and D2 create distinct offline edits from r; let D2 commit before D1's push.
cases.action: Deliver D1's stale operation and inspect the server receipt, remote head, and D1 local draft/outbox.
assert: The stale operation receives the frozen terminal conflict outcome and does not overwrite the remote head.
D1 retains its draft for resolution; it does not silently rebase or replace the already-sent wire operation.
A later user-approved resolution, if any, uses a new operation based on a confirmed revision.

cases.setup: Prepare a D1 delete at revision r while D2 updates the same synthetic entity to r+1 first.
cases.action: Deliver D1's stale delete and restart after its response.
assert: The stale delete cannot automatically advance to r+1 or delete the newer remote revision.
The local pending intent/draft remains available for explicit user confirmation; no new delete is emitted automatically.
The precise local mapping for ITEM_DELETED versus REVISION_CONFLICT remains governed by the frozen T16 DTO.

cases.setup: Retain one synthetic saved-item draft after a confirmed remote revision conflict; do not invoke any merge UI automatically.
cases.action: Observe the unresolved state, then separately exercise an explicit user-approved save-as-conflict-copy action after the resolution contract is frozen.
assert: The unresolved draft is not overwritten or dropped while awaiting a user decision.
If the user explicitly creates the spec's conflict copy, it uses a fresh entity/version identity and newly prepared encryption rather than copying server ciphertext under a changed ID.
Automatic merge rules, user prompts, and exact action/result mapping remain OPEN_QUESTION.

cases.setup: Persist an old-epoch synthetic outbox item and provide an isolated server state with a clearly newer workspace epoch.
cases.action: Attempt normal send and let the client process the epoch mismatch.
assert: The old operation is not automatically replayed into the new epoch or rewritten with a new epoch.
The draft/outbox source remains preserved for snapshot/recovery and explicit resolution.
No rollback or recovery result is inferred from a stale response alone.

cases.setup: Seed a clearly expired synthetic D1 lease, an old pending wire operation, and a server snapshot_required state.
cases.action: Attempt push with the old seenSeq and then follow the allowed snapshot-recovery entry path.
assert: Changing only seenSeq or blindly replaying the old outbox cannot reactivate the device or bypass snapshot recovery.
The old operation and its draft remain available while receipt/entity status is reconciled; absence of an old receipt is not proof of failure.
No lease equality/renewal timing is tested here; the fixture uses an unambiguously expired state.

cases.setup: Keep the active namespace at cursor afterSeq=80 with min_retained_seq=90, priorSeenHighWater=120, and a pending outbox operation for the same workspace epoch. Return the frozen 409 CURSOR_EXPIRED response; provide a valid snapshot H=90 and catchup changes through at least 120.
cases.action: Process CURSOR_EXPIRED, attempt recovery while observing sends, apply snapshot pages and catchup in a fresh namespace, then complete validation and publish.
assert: CURSOR_EXPIRED selects snapshot recovery; the active namespace, priorSeenHighWater=120, draft, and old outbox bytes remain preserved during recovery.
The old pending operation is not blindly replayed while cursor recovery is required; receipt/entity reconciliation remains necessary before any explicit retry or resolution.
Snapshot H=90 is not treated as rollback during baseline load; catchup reaches at least 120 before namespace and published cursor switch atomically.
Bootstrap ACK occurs only after the recovered namespace/cursor is committed and is bound to the matching snapshot state.
The exact local status mapping for CURSOR_EXPIRED remains OPEN_QUESTION under T17-OQ-04; this fixture asserts the frozen recovery action only.

cases.setup: After T07 freezes durable byte accounting, seed pendingBytes around outboxHardLimitBytes=209715200 and outboxSoftWarnBytes=52428800; include wire bytes and newly owned pending blob bytes.
cases.action: Attempt a new cloud mutation that falls under and over the hard cap while an existing operation is pending.
assert: The accounting input includes exact wire bytes plus newly owned pending BLOB bytes; already cloud-ready re-downloadable shared blobs are not charged twice as pending uploads.
Above the hard limit, a new cloud mutation is blocked without deleting or changing prior committed operations; at/below it, capacity handling follows the frozen limits/config contract.
The exact database/WAL/shared-reference durable charge formula remains gated by T07 and is not invented here.

cases.setup: Use an isolated synthetic profile with local-only capacity and cloud outbox capacity varied independently around local.totalBytes=524288000.
cases.action: Fill one budget at a time and attempt local-only and personal-cloud mutations without deleting protected saved items or pending operations.
assert: A cloud outbox hard-limit condition does not silently convert a personal-cloud edit to local-only or drop existing work.
Local-only mutations are governed by their own total local budget and do not create cloud outbox work.
Exact durable local.totalBytes charge components and WAL/shared-reference formula remain OPEN_QUESTION under T07.

references: 03 §2.2 local cache eviction and cloud tombstones
cases.setup: Seed one synthetic local cache/history copy eligible for local eviction and a separate cloud entity/outbox with no user delete action.
cases.action: Run local-only cache eviction/expiry and inspect generated cloud operations and the cloud tombstone state.
assert: Local LRU/history cache eviction removes only the local copy and does not create a cloud delete/tombstone operation.
The fixture does not confuse local cache expiry with the separately specified account history retention or explicit user deletion path.
No cloud deletion is inferred from a local TTL or local cache cleanup event.

cases.setup: Pause a synthetic push at a barrier after request bytes may have left the client but before any receipt is durably stored; cancel the client wait and restart.
cases.action: Inspect local state and reconcile through the frozen receipt/retry protocol without asserting whether the server received the request.
assert: Cancellation of the wait does not mutate/delete the possibly sent operation or claim remote cancellation.
The operation remains recoverable with its original identity/bytes until a receipt or other frozen resolution is recorded.
Exact cancellation API, user-visible result, and whether cancellation may abort only pre-send preparation remain OPEN_QUESTION.

cases.setup: Use a frozen synthetic pull DTO and a workspace with more than 50 changes; add a separate page that reaches 131072 exact response bytes first.
cases.action: Freeze upperSeq on the first page, commit an additional change during traversal, and fetch remaining pages using the same upperSeq.
assert: Pages obey the 50-item and 131072-byte configured limits; each toSeq is the final emitted change unless no changes remain through upperSeq.
The existing traversal does not include a later sequence beyond its frozen upperSeq; a new traversal can observe it.
A single summary too large to fit is excluded from behavior assertions until T16 freezes its policy.

cases.setup: Prepare one synthetic response page and an existing cursor; inject failure before local page/cursor commit and restart, then apply successfully and replay the same page.
cases.action: Inspect the entity projection and stored cursor after each path.
assert: A page and its cursor commit in one local transaction; failure cannot publish the new cursor without the page or the page without the cursor.
A replay after rollback is safe; a replay after commit is idempotent by the frozen entity/revision/seq rules.
No ACK is generated merely because an HTTP page was received.

cases.setup: Seed E1 with a locally confirmed newer revision while the durable cursor still precedes an older change for E1.
cases.action: Apply the older change page and then a current change page.
assert: The old change advances the processed sequence as allowed but does not overwrite the newer confirmed head or report rollback.
Same versionId with conflicting ciphertext is treated as a protocol anomaly and does not replace local content.
A missing entity alone is not treated as proof of malicious rollback.

cases.setup: Start requests at observed watermarks 98 and 99; deliver the newer response first and the older in-flight response second.
cases.action: Process both responses while recording each request's send-time watermark and the client's maximum observed watermark.
assert: A delayed response to an older request may be below the current watermark and does not trigger a false rollback alarm.
The stored maximum watermark never decreases when the delayed response arrives.
Rollback comparison uses the watermark captured when the corresponding current-state probe was sent.

cases.setup: Record a known same-epoch high watermark of 120, then issue a new current-state probe after that watermark is known.
cases.action: Return a server highWaterSeq below 120 for the newly issued probe.
assert: The client isolates/reports the specified remote rollback condition instead of lowering the known watermark or publishing older state.
This fixture is distinct from replaying a legitimate old snapshot or processing a delayed old response.

cases.setup: Prepare one page whose local transaction can be paused before commit and an isolated active device with appliedSeq=q.
cases.action: Attempt ACK before page commit, then commit the page/cursor and submit the resulting applied sequence; also try a same-epoch regression and a value above server lastSeq.
assert: Client ACK progress comes only from a locally committed cursor, not the time an HTTP response arrived.
Server ACK is monotonic within the same epoch and cannot exceed lastSeq; invalid ACK has no state effect.
A snapshot_required device cannot be activated by an ordinary ACK.

cases.setup: Persist one synthetic SENDING operation and provide a frozen successful receipt with committed revision/seq; inject local failure immediately before and after the receipt-confirmation transaction.
cases.action: Restart and inspect outbox row, receipt, confirmed revision/seq, and pending byte accounting.
assert: Before the local ACK transaction commits, the operation remains recoverable and its pending bytes are not released.
After commit, receipt plus confirmed revision/seq are durable before or atomically with clearing the queue item and releasing its pending accounting.
The test does not require ACKED to remain as a durable intermediate row; that row lifetime is OPEN_QUESTION.

cases.setup: Keep the current namespace at priorSeenHighWater=120; provide a synthetic reused snapshot at H=90 and catchup changes through at least 120.
cases.action: Write snapshot pages to a fresh recovery namespace, apply catchup after H, validate, and only then request namespace publish/bootstrap ACK.
assert: The current UI namespace and unsent drafts remain intact until snapshot pages and catchup reach at least priorSeenHighWater.
A legal older snapshot H=90 is not called rollback during baseline loading; versions are checked against prior seen state after catchup.
Namespace publication and published cursor are atomic, followed by bootstrap ACK tied to the matching snapshot/epoch/H.

cases.setup: Build a complete synthetic recovery namespace while retaining the old active namespace and pending outbox; inject failure immediately before and immediately after the publish transaction.
cases.action: Restart and inspect active namespace, published cursor, existing drafts/outbox, and recovery namespace lifecycle.
assert: Before the publish commit, readers continue using the old namespace and cursor; pending drafts/outbox are preserved.
After commit, namespace selection and published cursor agree on one recovered state; there is no mixed half-published view.
Recovery namespace resumability/cleanup details must follow a frozen T07/T19 interface and are not inferred by this case.

cases.setup: Create an unpublished recovery namespace with pending drafts/outbox, then independently expire its snapshot or change workspace epoch before publication.
cases.action: Attempt to continue/publish the old recovery baseline.
assert: The expired or wrong-epoch baseline is not published as current state.
Only the unpublished recovery baseline may be discarded/restarted; existing drafts and outbox are retained.
No exact cancellation/cleanup timing beyond the frozen snapshot contract is assumed.

cases.setup: Use synthetic epoch/revision/seq values 0, 1, 2^53, signed BIGINT max, and out-of-range/malformed strings after T06 freezes DTO rules.
cases.action: Round-trip values through outbox persistence, pull cursor, appliedSeq, and ACK representation.
assert: Valid Decimal values preserve exact digits without floating-point conversion; invalid or out-of-range input is rejected under the frozen DTO mapping.
The client never lowers a cursor/watermark as a side effect of parse failure.
No exact invalid-input error is asserted before T06/T16 contracts are frozen.

openQuestions.question: T06/T16 must freeze the exact PushOperationV1 canonical serialization, request hash scope, DTO versioning, and the bytes counted by wire_size before exact-byte/hash or transport compatibility assertions execute.
openQuestions.impact: The plan can require byte immutability across retry, but cannot invent canonical encoding or a hash-input set.

openQuestions.question: T07 must freeze the concrete SQLCipher schema/transaction and crash-durability test boundary for object refs, drafts, outbox, pendingBytes, and namespace/cursor publication; local.totalBytes durable charge components (including database/WAL/shared references) are also not frozen.
openQuestions.impact: Fixtures assert same-database transaction all-or-none where specified, but do not claim a particular fsync/power-loss guarantee or invent local byte arithmetic.

openQuestions.question: The spec lists ACKED as an outbox state and says the operation is cleared only after receipt plus confirmed revision/seq are recorded locally, but does not define whether ACKED persists as a row/journal or is transient within the same transaction that removes it.
openQuestions.impact: Assert atomic receipt/confirmed-state persistence before removal; do not require a particular intermediate ACKED row lifetime.

openQuestions.question: T16 must freeze operation receipt/push/pull/ACK DTO mappings and the client mapping of every terminal result (including ITEM_DELETED, COLLECTION_ENTRY_EXISTS, epoch/cursor/lease errors) to CONFLICT, BLOCKED, or recoverable draft state.
openQuestions.impact: Assert only outcomes explicitly frozen in 03; do not invent additional local status/error-code mappings.

openQuestions.question: The conflict-copy instruction freezes fresh identity and re-encryption for an explicit saved conflict copy, but merge behavior, user confirmation/UI flow, resolution of collection-entry conflicts, and whether/how a draft is discarded after a chosen resolution are not specified.
openQuestions.impact: Retain unresolved drafts and prohibit silent overwrite/auto-rebase; mark copy/merge behavior beyond fresh identity and encryption as gated.

openQuestions.question: Retry policy fixes exponential backoff with random jitter, Retry-After as a lower bound, and syncRetryMaxSeconds=300, but the jitter distribution, attempt schedule, and precise handling of malformed/oversized Retry-After are not frozen.
openQuestions.impact: Test identity/byte preservation and configured bounds only; do not assert exact timing until the policy is specified.

openQuestions.question: T17 requires snapshot recovery, but its direct dependency list does not include T19; exact snapshot request/page/bootstrap DTO ownership and the split between client recovery acceptance and T19 server snapshot acceptance need confirmation.
openQuestions.impact: Keep local recovery fixtures synthetic and contract-gated; do not add an implicit server dependency or claim end-to-end snapshot acceptance.

openQuestions.question: The spec does not fully define whether cancellation can stop only preparation/pre-send work or how an in-flight push cancellation is represented locally when delivery is ambiguous.
openQuestions.impact: An ambiguous possibly-sent operation must remain immutable and recoverable; do not claim remote cancellation or assume the request was not committed.

plannedCommands.gate: Wait for T07, T15, and T16 accepted; T06/T14 transitive gates and frozen DTO/storage interfaces required.
Wait for T07, T15, and T16 accepted; run only with the isolated T16 sync integration harness and frozen snapshot contract.
